title: Public Scorecard and Audit Trail
summary: What is published at the end of every term, and the five public indicators.

sections.heading: End-of-term publication
paragraphs: Each term concludes with: a release ledger (starting pool, release fraction, released units, four-channel split, closing pool); a bill and vote register; a Council action register; legal rulings and appeals; enacted uses; a chronicle of world events; and a scorecard.
Private goals remain private to their holders, but aggregated party progress is public.

sections.heading: The five indicators
paragraphs: These indicators are not a single ethical score. A party can succeed at private objectives while worsening the collective scorecard.

table.caption: Public indicators
rows: Share of the human population at or above the Charter baseline
Violations of bans found by the Tribunal
Share of voter groups whose highest priority received some resources
Assembly projects backed by most voter families
Reserve size and institutional standing of later generations

sections.heading: Current status
paragraphs: No scorecard has yet been published. The first scorecard will be issued in Week 4 of the First Term.

sections.heading: Closure of the simulation
paragraphs: The simulation has no mandatory final turn. With advance notice, moderators may close it and publish an epilogue grounded in the public ledger, the institutions that survived, and the accumulated physical and moral consequences of past choices.
